title: My Inktober Setup
summary: My setup for Inktober this year
content:
It's Inktober again which means I'm drawing one thing a day, in ink, from the official[1] prompt list. I'm tagging my posts with #Inktober and #Inktober2026 — these tag pages are flagged to render the images in a gallery instead of the usual notes pages. My first drawing is up as of this morning.

As much as I love Jeff the dinosaur from last year[2] it's too easy to fall back on "Jeff does/interacts with whatever the prompt is" so this year will be mostly Jeff-free. Last year my drawings were all over the place in terms of size so this year I bought a 12x12 Sakura sketchbook — I'll be using this exclusively for Inktober for the next few years. Unlike last year when I used Uni Pins, I'm a big Sakura Micron boy now. I talk more about this on this week's episode of The Pen Addict which will be out in a few hours.

One of the things with projects like this is I want to be consistent with how I'm posting stuff. Last year I would have to go back to the previous days post to see if I did a full stop or colon after the day number, did I put the prompt in quotes, what about the filename? So I set up two Alfred snippets — one for the filename and one for the post itself. Snippets is a feature I use a lot for other things.

# INKtober Filename
;inkf
# raw
inktober-2026-{date:dd}-
# becomes
inktober-2026-01-

# INKtober Post
;inkp
# raw
Day {date:dd} - {cursor}

![](https://cdn.rknight.me/site/2026/inktober-2026-{date:dd}-.jpg)
#becomes
Day 01 - 

![](https://cdn.rknight.me/site/2026/inktober-2026-01-.jpg)

  1. I've heard some not great things about the official folks and "licensing" the name but nothing substantial so I'm sticking with it ⤾

  2. And let's not even talk about Knobgate ⤾
